title: Bounded constructible integral p-adic module complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be a finite intermediate extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm induced from the fixed algebraic closure, and let $X$ be a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. Write $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:\lVert x\rVert\leq1\}$, let $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ be the condensed ring of continuous $\mathcal O_E$-valued functions on profinite spaces, and let $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ be its inverse image on the pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. In the ordinary derived category of internal $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-modules, the object property of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] is triangulated. Here constructibility is finite stratified local finite presentation; no derived completeness condition is added.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1),(3), as implemented in integralConstructible_serre; passage to bounded cohomology by the weak Serre homology-property theorem

proof.text: Give the finite subfield E of the fixed algebraic closure the induced norm. Norm multiplicativity, scalar-tower compatibility and the fact that the algebraic-closure norm extends the p-adic norm give a NormedAlgebra structure over Q_l. The valuation ring defined by restricting the algebraic-closure valuation is definitionally the norm-at-most-one subring continuousIntegers. Hence the continuous-function condensed coefficient ring integralCoeff and the existing padicIntegersRingObj, including their ring-object structures, are definitionally equal. This also identifies their pullbacks to X.
